title: Soviet version of Operation Paperclip

tellings.quote: But the Russians had their own version of paperclip. And the Russians brought more than 3,000 scientists and their families into Russia,

plain: After the Second World War, the Soviet Union ran its own version of Operation Paperclip, the US program that brought German scientists to America, and took more than 3,000 scientists and their families into Russia. The author Peter Levenda tells this, drawing on a book called Secret Machines. It shows that the race for German know-how was not only an American one.
